stem: When \( 10^{8} \) electrons are transferred from one conductor to another, a potential difference of 10 \( V \) appears between the conductors. Find the capacitance of the two conductors.
solution:
Given :
Number of electrons \( n = 10^{8} \)
\( V = 10 \) volt

\( \therefore \) charge transferred
\( Q = ne = 10^{8} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \)
\( (\because e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \) C)
\( = 1.6 \times 10^{-11} \) C

\( \therefore \) Capacitance between two conductors
\( C = \dfrac{Q}{V} = \dfrac{1.6 \times 10^{-11}}{10} = 1.6 \times 10^{-12} \) F

stem: From the figure given below find the value of the capacitance \( C \) if the equivalent capacitance between A and B is to be \( 1\,\mu\text{F} \). All other capacitors are in micro farad.
solution:
Given :
\( C_1 = 8\,\mu\text{F} \), \( C_2 = 4\,\mu\text{F} \), \( C_3 = 1\,\mu\text{F} \), \( C_4 = 4\,\mu\text{F} \), \( C_5 = 4\,\mu\text{F} \)

The effective capacitance of \( C_4 \) and \( C_5 \) in parallel
\( = C_4 + C_5 = 4 + 4 = 8\,\mu\text{F} \)

The effective capacitance of \( C_3 \) and \( 8\,\mu\text{F} \) in series
\( = \dfrac{1 \times 8}{1 + 8} = \dfrac{8}{9}\,\mu\text{F} \)

The capacitance \( 8\,\mu\text{F} \) is in parallel with the series combination of \( C_1 \) and \( C_2 \). Their effective combination is

\( \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} + \dfrac{8}{9} \Rightarrow \dfrac{8 \times 4}{12} + \dfrac{8}{9} \Rightarrow \dfrac{32}{9}\,\mu\text{F} \)

This capacitance of \( \dfrac{32}{9}\,\mu\text{F} \) is in series with \( C \) and their effective capacitance is given to be \( 1\,\mu\text{F} \)

\( \dfrac{\dfrac{32}{9} \times C}{\dfrac{32}{9} + C} = 1 \)

\( \therefore \dfrac{32}{9} \times C = \dfrac{32}{9} + C \)

\( = 1.392\,\mu\text{F} \)

subtopic: Parallel Plate Capacitor with a Dielectric
stem:
A parallel plate capacitor has an area of 4 cm\( ^2 \) and a plate separation of 2 mm
(i) Calculate its capacitance
(ii) What is its capacitance if the space between the plates is filled completely with a dielectric having dielectric constant of constant 6.7.
solution:
Given
\( A = 4 \) cm\( ^2 = 4 \times 10^{-4} \) m\( ^2 \)
\( d = 2 \) mm \( = 2 \times 10^{-3} \) m
\( \varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \) C\( ^2 \) / Nm\( ^2 \)

(i) Capacitance \( C = \dfrac{A\varepsilon_0}{d} \)
\( = \dfrac{8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 4 \times 10^{-4}}{2 \times 10^{-3}} = 1.77 \times 10^{-12} \) F

(ii) Capacitance \( C' = \dfrac{A\varepsilon_0 k}{d} \)
\( = \dfrac{8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 4 \times 10^{-4} \times 6.7}{2 \times 10^{-3}} \)
\( = 11.86 \times 10^{-12} \) F

subtopic: Parallel Plate Capacitor with a Dielectric
stem: In a capacitor of capacitance \( 20\,\mu\text{F} \), the distance between the plates is 2 mm. If a dielectric slab of width 1 mm and dielectric constant 2 is inserted between the plates, what is the new capacitance?
solution:
Given
\( C = 20\,\mu\text{F} = 20 \times 10^{-6} \) F
\( d = 2 \) mm \( = 2 \times 10^{-3} \) m
\( t = 1 \times 10^{-3} \) m
\( k = 2 \)

\( C = \dfrac{A\varepsilon_0}{d} \) and \( C' = \dfrac{A\varepsilon_0}{d - t + \dfrac{t}{k}} \)

\( \Rightarrow \dfrac{C}{C'} = \dfrac{d - t + \dfrac{t}{k}}{d} \)

\( \Rightarrow \dfrac{20}{C'} = \dfrac{\left(2 \times 10^{-3} - 1 \times 10^{-3} + \dfrac{1 \times 10^{-3}}{2}\right)}{2 \times 10^{-3}} \)

\( \Rightarrow C' = 26.67\,\mu\text{F} \)

stem: A parallel plate air capacitor has a capacitance of \( 3 \times 10^{-9} \) Farad. A slab of dielectric constant 3 and thickness 3 cm completely fills the space between the plates. The potential difference between the plates is maintained constant at 400 volt. What is the change in the energy of capacitor if the slab is removed?
solution:
Energy stored in the capacitor with air

\( E_a = \dfrac{1}{2}CV^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 10^{-9} \times (400)^2 \)
\( = 24 \times 10^{-5} \) J

when the slab of dielectric constant 3 is introduced between the plates of the capacitor, the capacitance of the capacitor increases to
\( C' = kC \)
\( C' = 3 \times 3 \times 10^{-9} = 9 \times 10^{-9} \) F

Energy stored in the capacitor with the dielectric \( (E_d) \)

\( E_d = \dfrac{1}{2}C'V^2 \)

\( E_d = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 10^{-9} \times (400)^2 \)
\( = 72 \times 10^{-5} \) J

Change in energy \( = E_d - E_a = (72 - 24) \times 10^{-5} \)
\( = 48 \times 10^{-5} \) J

There is, therefore, an increase in the energy on introducing the slab of dielectric material.
